key_insight: A surrogate-assisted inverse-design workflow can efficiently tune an all-oxide 1D grating emitter to produce a high, narrowband thermal emission peak aligned for thermophotovoltaic use.
engineering_relevance: Using oxide-only layers on sapphire improves high-temperature robustness versus metal-dielectric emitters while targeting better spectral matching to the TPV cell bandgap.
method: Train ExtraTrees surrogate models on FDTD-generated spectra from varied layer thicknesses and grating period.
Use Bayesian optimization on a penalty-augmented objective that enforces high peak emissivity while minimizing FWHM and maximizing in-band fraction.
Validate the optimized design with direct FDTD simulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a prediction target set including peak emissivity, peak wavelength, FWHM, and in-band fraction, with the optimized structure subsequently confirmed by FDTD.
watch_item: Performance depends on the surrogate's training coverage, so the optimization may miss designs outside the sampled thickness/period space or require careful fabrication tolerance control.
paper_title: Surrogate-Assisted Inverse Design and Temperature-Dependent Electrothermal Analysis of an All-Oxide Narrowband Thermophotovoltaic Emitter
